title: Cohort-based TTL and automated evidence export for request artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and deliver a cohort-driven TTL model for prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics plus an automated evidence export pipeline. The goal is to allow tenancy- and route-aware retention cohorts (eg. short-lived dev, 30-day standard, 7-year regulatory) with deterministic export bundles for audits. This ticket covers policy model, route/route-pattern UI knobs, export/playbook automation, and acceptance criteria for data residency enforcement during exports.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can create retention cohorts and assign them to routes or route patterns in Console
System applies cohort TTL to incoming request artifacts (prompts/responses/logs/metrics) and enforces eviction according to cohort rules
Evidence export CLI/webhook can produce a signed bundle (per-tenant, per-period) that includes hashed manifests and optional PII redaction metadata
Export respects tenant data residency constraints: bundles are assembled within the chosen region and signed using customer KMS when requested
Audit playbook and attestation document generated for each export including SHA256 checksums and chain-of-custody metadata
E2E tests verify retention and export behavior for three sample cohorts (dev-7d, prod-90d, regulated-7y) and legal hold overrides
tasks: Finalize cohort schema and retention expression language (TTL + sampling + sensitivity override)
Design Console UX for cohort creation, assignment, and preview of projected storage impact
Implement per-route cohort assignment and enforcement in request router (runtime tagging + metadata propagation)
Build evidence export pipeline: snapshotter, compacting, signing, and export artifact packing
Add residency-aware export execution (region-local snapshot + signed manifest) and KMS integration hooks
Create acceptance/QA test harness and CI job to validate exports and legal-hold behavior
Document operational runbook and incident rollback steps for accidental over-retention or early purge
risks: Complex interaction between sampling (to reduce cost) and evidentiary completeness for audits
Performance impact of snapshotting high-throughput routes during export windows
Edge cases where multi-region tenants have mixed residency rules requiring split exports
Legal hold override must reliably prevent purge even under autoscaling/purge storms
KMS integration increases blast radius for export failures if keys are misconfigured
